title: The lay apostolate (Apostolicam Actuositatem)
hook: laypeople bring the gospel into every part of life
tomorrow: is mission a job for a few, or what a whole church is?

segments.voice: Yesterday the decree on ecumenism held two instincts together: real differences, and a real family. Rightly called brothers.

Five in the morning at a bakery. Flour hangs in the air, the ovens tick as they heat, and the dough that went into the bins last night has quietly doubled. Nobody in there is preaching. Somebody is humming, maybe. Does a shift like that count as part of a church's mission? Vatican II's decree on the laity answers with a baker's word.
screen: `FLOUR IN THE AIR.` → `THE DOUGH HAS DOUBLED.` → `DOES A SHIFT COUNT?`

segments.voice: Start with the word. An apostolate is a mission, a sending. And the decree, Apostolicam Actuositatem, opens with a surprise about who gets sent. The Christian calling, it says, is by its very nature also a calling to the apostolate. Not an extra for the very devout. Built in. Then where. Laypeople, the decree says, live in the middle of the world and its ordinary business, and they're called to work for the world's holiness from the inside, like leaven. Jesus used the same picture: "The kingdom of heaven is like to leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, until the whole was leavened." Leaven doesn't stand apart from the bread. You can't see it once it's mixed in. You can only see what it does. Then how. Family cares, work and the rest of daily life, the decree says, don't sit off to one side of a person's spiritual life. Lived in the right spirit, they're part of it. So the bakery counts. So does the classroom, the truck cab, the night shift at the hospital, the kitchen at six with lunches to pack. The laity share, in their own way, in the mission of the whole Church, right where they stand.
screen: `AN APOSTOLATE IS A SENDING.` · `BUILT INTO EVERY CHRISTIAN CALLING.` · `LIKE LEAVEN, FROM THE INSIDE.` · `DAILY LIFE IS PART OF IT.` · then, large: `WHERE YOU ARE.`

segments.voice: If there's something to eat or drink within reach, bread, coffee, an orange, bring it close and breathe it in. Somebody grew it, baked it, hauled it, stocked it: a whole chain of ordinary work ending in your hands. Taste it slowly, and let that work be part of the quiet.
The lay apostolate. The mission laypeople carry, like leaven, into family, work and public life.
Your line: where you are. The kitchen, the job and the bus ride home all count. Back tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholic laypeople live this out in their families and jobs, and many also serve in parish ministries, charities and lay movements.

apostolate.meaning: a mission or sending to spread the gospel

Apostolicam Actuositatem.meaning: Vatican II's decree on the mission of laypeople

leaven.meaning: yeast or starter dough that makes bread rise

Laypeople.meaning: members of the Church who aren't ordained
